content: I am on Windows 11, and I find that it takes several minutes for Lean to load. I am loading the MathLib library, but my friend who uses Linux uses the same package and has a load time under 30 seconds. What may be causing the load time to be significantly slower?
Possible answer: Microsoft Defender.
Okay. What should I be looking for in Microsoft Defender? I wasn't able to find anything related to Lean or VS Code
Switch it off (or if you can't switch it off, tell it to stop scanning the drive where all your files are) and see if it makes a difference.

Go to Security

Then virus and account protection

then manage settings > exclusions

and add the directories to exclude

I don't feel comfortable with turning my Microsoft Defender off completely.

What directories do I exclude? I don't know which ones would be necessary for Lean to work

I am suggesting that you turn it off completely for 5 minutes and see if it solves the problem, because if it doesn't then we're wasting our time discussing it. There are several reasons why lean might be slow, I just started with a common one.

This was the solution for my work MacBook (which my employer had installed defender on) and I could not work out which directories to ignore to make the problem go away, but when I stopped scanning my home directory for 5 minutes it immediately became clear that defender was the problem.
For others the problem has been: other antivirus software, no mathlib oleans, slow hard drive, not enough RAM

There are also rare reasons like weird VS Code settings etc etc. All these are debuggable, there are technical questions which people can ask and where you can do an experiment and report back if it helps. But the experiment for defender is "switch the bloody thing off for 5 minutes and see if it solves the problem"
If it does then we can experiment more and try and find a better solution than switching it off completely

Sorry, computer settings scare me since things can go very wrong very quickly, and I don't know enough about computers to know what I'm doing

Now that I look at it further, my computer only has Windows Defender Firewall and Windows Security. Which one do you mean? The former seems unrelated

I'm afraid I don't know the first thing about Windows. All I know is that when Windows users come to this forum saying "lean is weirdly slow for me" then a common first step for debugging is "switch off your antivirus". I guess you could just ask an LLM which one of these is an antivirus
Don't you see the screenshots i posted ? it's on the same page to disable it
disable is only temporary as the description says.
I'm trying it out, and it still is very slow
So what exactly is slow? What actions do you do and then what happens and how long does it take?

It seems to be building several files, and each file takes about a second to load. The screenshot shows one of the messages it shows. This particular upload didn't take 11 seconds, so I don't know what the (11 s) is for, but some of them do take more than 10 seconds.
Are you fetching the cache?
What is the cache?
I think that I should add that I was trying to update my MathLib version (though not successfully), but I've had similarly slow load times when opening files
What do you mean by "update"? Are you saying you ran lake update?
you are obviously missing the Mathlib cache. on vscode fetch the mathlib cache:

Yaël Dillies said:

What do you mean by "update"? Are you saying you ran lake update?

It's complicated. When I was trying to update my Lean version, I tried the command lake update, and it told me that I already had the latest version of Lean. I then went through a journey of trying different buttons in VS Code that all seemed to do nothing or gave an ominous warnings that I turned back from. I also tried changing the lean-toolchain file, which caused nearly all of the issues that I'm running into now
Have you tried fetching the mathlib build cache , like shown on my last screenshot ?
I would delete everything and start again.

Alfredo Moreira-Rosa said:

Have you tried fetching the mathlib build cache , like shown on my last screenshot ?

I'm trying this now. It's taking a minute or so to "[Fetch Mathlib Build Cache] Fetching Mathlib build artifact cache"
When doing so, it seemed to stop the prior process it was doing

Right now you seem to be saying "I downloaded mathlib and then I did a bunch of random things which changed the files and now I'm in a mess", so one solution would be to delete everything, create a new project following the instructions on the lean website, don't type any system commands or anything like that, and see if this solves your problems
It's now done importing the cache, and now I'm restarting the file
It's done restarting now, and it looks like I resolved the extraneous issues that were complicating matters. I'm going to test restarting the file
Update: "Restart File" process completed. It took 14 minutes, which is about how long it typically takes for me. I'm going to try it again with Windows Security off

It seems that Windows Security was causing the problem in the particular case when I press "Restart File", but not in the other contexts that caused very slow load times. I'm still not sure why there were slow load times in the other contexts
This might be because you typed lake update, which will have messed up your cache.
